# agent-qa.yaml reference

<!-- Generated by `npm run schema` from src/core/config/schema.ts. Edit the descriptions there, not this file. -->

agent-qa.yaml: Agent-QA's settings. Secrets appear only as ${env:NAME} or ${keychain:NAME} references. `agent-qa init` writes a starting file ([getting-started.md](getting-started.md)), and `agent-qa doctor` checks it. Editors that read JSON Schema (VS Code with the YAML extension) show these descriptions as you type, from the `# yaml-language-server: $schema=…` line at the top of the file.

A secret reference is `${env:NAME}` (an environment variable) or `${keychain:NAME}` (your OS keychain, under the service `sf-agent-qa`). A secret written in the file itself is refused.

## `version`

The version of this file's format. Always 1. Required.

## `project`

About the project. Optional.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `project.name` | text | required | A name for the project. Not used by any workflow yet. |

## `atlassian`

Jira and Confluence Cloud. Needed by every workflow that reads requirements. Optional.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `atlassian.site` | URL | required | Your Jira Cloud site, such as https://acme.atlassian.net. |
| `atlassian.email` | text | required | The email of the Atlassian account the API token belongs to. It is personal data: prefer ${env:ATLASSIAN_EMAIL}, so it stays out of git. |
| `atlassian.token` | secret reference | required | The Atlassian API token, as a secret reference. |
| `atlassian.confluence` | section |  | Where `document` publishes to Confluence. |
| `atlassian.confluence.spaceKey` | text | required | The key of the space documents are published to. |
| `atlassian.confluence.parentPageId` | text |  | The id of the page that published documents go under. Without it, the page is created with no parent, and Confluence places it in the space (on Confluence Cloud, under the space's home page). |
| `atlassian.jira` | section |  | How requirements are read from Jira. Every key has a default. |
| `atlassian.jira.acceptanceCriteriaField` | text |  | The field that holds acceptance criteria, by id or name. Default: a field named like acceptance criteria, else the criteria in the description. |
| `atlassian.jira.extraFields` | list of text |  | More text fields to read into each requirement, by id or name. |
| `atlassian.jira.maxDepth` | whole number (0 to 5) |  | Levels of child issues read below each input issue (epic, story, sub-task). Default 3. |
| `atlassian.jira.maxIssues` | whole number (1 to 500) |  | The most issues read in one run. Default 100. |
| `atlassian.jira.followLinks` | true or false |  | Read linked issues, one level out. Default true. |
| `atlassian.jira.followLinkedChildren` | true or false |  | Also read the children of linked issues. Default true. |
| `atlassian.jira.maxPages` | whole number (0 to 100) |  | The most linked Confluence pages read in one run. Default 20. |

## `xray`

Xray Cloud, where test cases and Test Executions are written. Optional.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `xray.clientId` | text | required | The Xray API key's client id, or a secret reference to it. |
| `xray.clientSecret` | secret reference | required | The Xray API key's client secret, as a secret reference. |
| `xray.projectKey` | text | required | The Jira project the tests are created in, such as QA. |
| `xray.baseUrl` | URL |  | The Xray Cloud region's URL. Default https://xray.cloud.getxray.app. |
| `xray.priorities` | section |  | The Jira priority name for each test priority, such as `P1: Highest`. A priority left out isn't set. |
| `xray.priorities.P1` | text |  | The Jira priority name for P1. |
| `xray.priorities.P2` | text |  | The Jira priority name for P2. |
| `xray.priorities.P3` | text |  | The Jira priority name for P3. |
| `xray.priorities.P4` | text |  | The Jira priority name for P4. |
| `xray.linkType` | text | `Test` | The Jira link type from each test to its requirement. Default Test (tests / is tested by). |
| `xray.attachScreenshots` | true or false | `false` | Attach Playwright's screenshots to the tests of a Test Execution, passed or failed. Off by default: a screenshot can't be masked, so what the page showed (names, record data) goes to Xray as it is. |
| `xray.executionDates` | section |  | The Test Execution's own start and end date fields, which Xray doesn't set from the results: Jira custom fields, with each field's type. |
| `xray.executionDates.start` | section |  | The field for the execution's start. |
| `xray.executionDates.start.field` | text | required | The Jira custom field id, such as customfield_10505. |
| `xray.executionDates.start.type` | `date`, `datetime` | `datetime` | `date` for a field that holds a day (the UTC day is written), `datetime` for a date and time. |
| `xray.executionDates.end` | section |  | The field for the execution's end. |
| `xray.executionDates.end.field` | text | required | The Jira custom field id, such as customfield_10505. |
| `xray.executionDates.end.type` | `date`, `datetime` | `datetime` | `date` for a field that holds a day (the UTC day is written), `datetime` for a date and time. |

## `git`

Your git host: read for pull request context, and used to open pull requests from CI. Optional.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `git.platform` | `github`, `gitlab`, `azure-devops` | required | Where the repository is hosted. |
| `git.repo` | text | required | owner/name on GitHub, organization/project/repository on Azure DevOps, the project's full path (group/subgroup/project) on GitLab. |
| `git.token` | secret reference | required | A token that can read pull requests and open one, as a secret reference. |
| `git.baseUrl` | URL |  | The REST API root for a self-hosted server, such as https://HOST/api/v3 on GitHub Enterprise Server. Default: the cloud service. |

## `salesforce`

Salesforce sign-in for `explore` and the generated tests: the JWT bearer flow of an External Client App, one user per role. Nothing is stored: each sign-in makes a single-use URL. Optional.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `salesforce.baseUrl` | URL | required | The org's My Domain URL, such as https://acme--uat.sandbox.my.salesforce.com. |
| `salesforce.auth` | `"jwt"` | `jwt` | How users sign in. Only jwt: the OAuth JWT bearer flow, which no MFA prompt stops. |
| `salesforce.loginUrl` | URL | `https://login.salesforce.com` | https://login.salesforce.com, or https://test.salesforce.com for a sandbox. |
| `salesforce.audience` | URL |  | The JWT assertion's audience. Default: https://test.salesforce.com for test.salesforce.com and sandbox My Domains, else https://login.salesforce.com. |
| `salesforce.clientId` | text | required | The External Client App's consumer key, or a secret reference to it. |
| `salesforce.privateKey` | secret reference |  | The app's private key (PEM), as a secret reference. Give this or privateKeyFile. |
| `salesforce.privateKeyFile` | text |  | The path to the private key file (PEM), outside the repo, or a secret reference holding the path. Give this or privateKey. |
| `salesforce.users` | map of name to text | required | The Salesforce username for each role, such as `StoreManager-FRA: user@acme.com.uat`, or a secret reference. At least one. |

## `models`

The models that answer from the CLI and CI. In an IDE, the IDE's own model answers (docs/models.md). Optional.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `models.default` | text | required | The model for every step, as provider:model, such as anthropic:claude-sonnet-5-5, unless models.workflows or --model names another. |
| `models.allowed` | list of text |  | The models that may run, as provider:model or provider:*. A model outside the shipped catalog runs, with a doctor warning. |
| `models.workflows` | map of name to text |  | A model for one workflow, by workflow id, such as `scripts: anthropic:claude-opus-5-5`. |
| `models.keys` | map of name (`anthropic`, `openai`, `mistral`, `xai`, `google`, `openrouter`, `litellm`) to secret reference |  | The API key for each provider, as a secret reference. Default: the provider's usual variable, such as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. |
| `models.endpoints` | map of name (`anthropic`, `openai`, `mistral`, `xai`, `google`, `openrouter`, `litellm`) to URL |  | The base URL for a provider: OpenRouter, or your LiteLLM gateway. |

## `masking`

How personal data is masked before a model sees it (docs/security.md). Optional.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `masking.restoreOnWrite` | true or false | `false` | Put the real values back into what is written to Xray and Confluence, on an approved write. Off: they receive the tokens as they are. |
| `masking.detectors` | list of `email`, `phone`, `iban`, `card`, `national-id`, `name`, `address`, `ip` |  | The detectors that run. Default: all. `address` is accepted but has no detector yet. |
| `masking.fields` | map of name to list of text |  | Fields always replaced whole, by source, such as `jira: [customfield_10042, "Customer phone"]`. |
| `masking.languages` | list of `en`, `fr`, `es`, `de`, `pt`, `nl`, `it`, `ar`, `zh` |  | The languages whose name lists find names that no people field lists. Default: all nine. |
| `masking.presidio` | section |  | Accepted and checked by doctor, but nothing sends text to Presidio yet. |
| `masking.presidio.url` | URL or null | required | The Presidio analyzer's URL. |

## `policy`

What Agent-QA may write outside its run folder, and what it asks you first (docs/security.md). Optional.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `policy.writes` | section | see its keys | allow, ask or deny for each target. |
| `policy.writes.xray` | `allow`, `ask`, `deny` | `ask` | Creating and updating test cases and Test Executions. In CI, ask is denied. |
| `policy.writes.confluence` | `allow`, `ask`, `deny` | `ask` | Publishing a document. In CI, ask is denied. |
| `policy.writes.testCode` | `allow`, `ask`, `deny` | `ask` | Writing or deleting files in your repo. In CI, anything but deny leaves the code as a pull request, never a push. |
| `policy.writes.jira` | `allow`, `ask`, `deny` | `deny` | Reserved: nothing writes to Jira. |
| `policy.writes.commands` | `allow`, `ask`, `deny` | `ask` | Running the commands the framework profile lists (tests, type check) in your repo. In CI, anything but deny allows. |

## `harness`

Your own cases for `agent-qa harness`. Without this section, it runs the shipped synthetic cases (docs/harness.md). Optional.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `harness.sources` | list | required | Where the cases come from: `- fixtures: path/to/cases`. |
| `harness.sources[].fixtures` | text | one of these | A folder of harness cases. |
| `harness.sources[].jira` | section | one of these | Accepted, but skipped for now: a Jira source has no known seeds to check. |
| `harness.sources[].jira.jql` | text | required | A JQL filter. |
| `harness.seededPersonalData` | text |  | A file of the planted values to look for. Default: the shipped seeds. |

## `playwright`

A local web app, for `explore` without Salesforce. Optional.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `playwright.baseUrl` | URL | `http://localhost:3000` | A local app for `explore` to drive when there is no salesforce section. |
| `playwright.testDir` | text | `tests` | Not used: the reviewed framework profile says where the tests are. |
| `playwright.profile` | text | `.agent-qa/framework-profile.json` | Not used: the reviewed profile is always agent-qa.profile.json at the project root. |
